rationale: The unknowns are practical: whether nurses can deliver the intervention to most screen-positive patients before discharge (c1 suggests they can elsewhere), whether patients can be reached after discharge (c2 suggests about half), and whether patients accept the conversation (c3). A single-ward feasibility study with pre-stated progression criteria answers these without claiming effectiveness. The unverified landmark lead is not used.
alternatives: Controlled comparison of drinking outcomes (refused: effectiveness cannot be estimated before delivery and retention are known)
Audit of current alcohol care only (refused: would not test delivery of the intervention)
Referral pathway to the community alcohol team without ward sessions
guidelines: CONSORT extension for pilot and feasibility studies (as far as applicable to a non-comparative study)
whyNotMoreComplex: A comparative design would need a sample the ward cannot recruit in nine months and would be premature while follow-up rates are unknown.

decision.statement: Run a single-ward feasibility study of nurse-delivered screening and a two-session brief intervention, judged against pre-stated progression criteria for screening, uptake, delivery and three-month follow-up.
decision.question: Should the ward test whether nurse-delivered alcohol screening and brief intervention are feasible before any larger evaluation?

criteria.text: Delivery by ward nurses and acceptable timing are plausible from retrieved evidence, while follow-up is uncertain enough to need local estimates.
A local estimate of screening, uptake and follow-up already exists for this ward.

gates.requirement: Ward manager approval of screening and two sessions within named-nurse shifts
gates.evidence: Approval WM-4A-2026-11 (January to September 2027), supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Research ethics committee favourable opinion on the feasibility protocol

alternatives: Referral pathway only, without ward sessions
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3 from retrieved records; the ethics opinion is unknown, so the action stays blocked after acceptance.

summary: Feasibility study recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims and waits for the ethics opinion.
